title: Resumable schema linter and SDK sprint notes
body:
Context
------
Short: we need a lightweight CI + dev-time linter that validates streaming/partial/structured outputs against a small, expressive schema DSL so SDKs (mobile + web + server) can implement deterministic resume, client-side reconciliation, and helpful developer errors instead of subtle runtime breakage.

Why now
------
- Increasing number of tool-calling flows return partial JSON frames; different clients parse/merge slightly differently -> flaky resume behavior.
- We've had 3 customer incidents in Q3 where a schema change in a hosted model caused SDKs to either hang waiting for fields, or to accept broken partial frames and surface corrupted UI.
- Product goal for H1: reduce streaming resume regressions by 80% and make local dev feedback immediate.

Success criteria (measurable)
---------------------------
- Linter rules run in PRs that touch response schemas / router rules; blocking on high-confidence regressions.
- Local dev experience: editor/cli warning within 1s for schema mismatches (VSCode extension or pre-commit).
- SDKs adopt the linter output mapping: at least 2 official SDKs implement deterministic resume logic using linter-derived metadata (server-js, android).
- Post-rollout: < 1 resume-related incident per quarter.

Scope & constraints
-------------------
In-scope this sprint:
- Define minimal schema DSL (stream-safe subset of JSON Schema + extra streaming markers).
- Implement prototype linter as a python/ts CLI and GitHub action.
- Mapping guide for SDKs: how to translate linter metadata to resume heuristics (prefix anchors, idempotency tokens, optional deltas).
- Telemetry contract: what to emit when a client rejects a frame or uses fallback.

Out-of-scope (for now):
- Auto-migration tools that rewrite prompts or user payloads to match new schema.
- Deep model-output synthesis to canonicalize frames (we will detect and warn; synthesis is separate).

Design sketch: schema DSL (sketch)
--------------------------------
Goals: small, readable, stream-friendly. The linter must be able to reason about partial frames and whether they form a valid continuation.
Principles:
- Explicit "frame anchors" (fields that must appear in the first frame)
- "patchable" marker for objects that can be delivered incrementally (apply-merge semantics)
- optional/required semantics that are tolerant to streaming (e.g., a field can be 'deferred' until end)

Example DSL (human format)
- response: object
  - session_id: string (anchor)
  - steps: list[patchable object]
    - step_id: string (anchor)
    - status: enum[pending,complete] (deferred)
    - content: patchable-markdown
  - metadata: object (optional)

Notes:
- 'anchor' indicates the field must be present in the initial frame or the resume cannot reconcile.
- 'patchable' indicates the SDK should apply incremental merges (KV merge, list append semantics where applicable).
- DSL intentionally lighter than full JSON Schema to be fast and less surprising.

Linter rule categories (proposed)
--------------------------------
- Anchors missing in first frame: ERROR (high) - fix server/model contract or SDK cannot resume safely.
- Conflicting anchor types across versions (string -> object): ERROR (high).
- Patchable field declared but frames include an overwrite instead of incremental patches: WARNING (medium) - could cause UI flicker.
- Non-deterministic ordering of arrays declared as 'ordered' vs 'unordered': WARNING.
- Deprecated field presence without migration hint: INFO.

How to treat partial frames
--------------------------
- Linter must be able to simulate a stream: given an ordered list of frames (0..N), is there a path to a valid final object? We will run two checks: local single-frame sanity + multi-frame converge test (best-effort).
- For CI GH action, we run single-frame checks on any changed schema and rerun converge tests for a handful of recent real-world session traces (sampled).

Developer+SDK ergonomics
------------------------
- CLI: redwood-schema-lint check <schema.yaml> --sample-traces traces/  (returns exit code, machine parseable JSON output)
- Editor: quick diagnostics on anchor/patchable mistakes.
- SDK adapter: a small generated JSON that maps field -> resume strategy (anchor|patch|deferred|discard) that SDKs ingest during init to set parsing rules and telemetry tags.

Example generated mapping (human):
- session_id -> anchor
- steps -> patchable-list(merge-by-step_id)
- metadata -> deferred

Integration points
------------------
- Model onboarding: when we publish new model/service response schemas in the catalog, linter validation is a gating step.
- Router/edges: store the generated mapping as a lightweight JSON on model artifacts so runtime can attach schema-version id in trace headers.
- SDKs: use header schema-version to fetch mapping (or use embedded mapping from client build) and enforce local parsing rules.

Telemetry plan
--------------
- Events the SDK emits (standardized):
  - schema_mismatch.blocking (error) -> includes schema_version, field, expected, actual, session_id
  - schema_mismatch.warning -> for non-blocking issues
  - resume_applied -> when a resume uses patch semantics successfully
  - resume_fallback -> when client falls back to full-reload or re-request
- Sampling: blocking events always sampled; warnings sampled at 1% default.
- Add a runtime label: schema_source = [embedded|fetched|none] so we can track drift when SDKs run with stale mappings.

Testing and QA
--------------
- Unit tests for linter rules, with >100 synthetic examples (anchor present/absent, patches, reorderings).
- Integration test: run linter against 50 sampled production traces (anonymized) to ensure converge test passes.
- SDK harness: build a small replay runner that consumes mock frames and asserts that the SDKs produce identical final objects under both resume-enabled and naive strategies.

Rollout plan
------------
1) Internal alpha: run linter in non-blocking mode on infra PRs for 2 squads (console+hosted-runtime) for 2 weeks.
2) Beta: enable blocking rule for anchor-missing on model schema PRs and announce SDK mapping artifact format.
3) Gradual enforcement: block on high severity errors only; monitor telemetry for false positives.

Open questions / tradeoffs (notes)
--------------------------------
- DSL expressiveness vs adoption friction: keep tiny + iterate. If we try to cover every streaming edge case we won't ship.
- Should we auto-generate mapping from JSON Schema (with annotations) or require hand-authored DSL? Hybrid seems best: annotate JSON Schema fields with streaming hints and run the linter to synthesize mapping.
- Where to store mapping: model artifact (preferred) vs CDN (for quick SDK updates). Model artifact means mapping always co-located with model version.
- Backwards compatibility: if mapping changes, should SDKs automatically switch mid-session? No — require schema-version bump and full session restart or explicit compatibility rules.

Immediate TODOs (this sprint)
---------------------------
- [x] Draft DSL doc (this file)
- [ ] Prototype CLI (Luca) - target: basic anchor/type checks by 2025-11-26
- [ ] GH action (Priya) - wire simple check for INFR-724 by 2025-11-28
- [ ] SDK mapping spec (Ethan) - publish on Confluence and open PR for server-js adapter by 2025-12-02
- [ ] Telemetry schema draft for events (Maya) - push draft to telemetry repo by 2025-11-25

Notes / workshop fragments
-------------------------
- Quick dev workflow idea: when a model author updates schema, run 'schema-lint --explain' that emits a short natural language description of what changed from previous version (e.g., "session_id changed from optional to anchor"). This helps non-technical product folks review.
- Consider a low-level 'strictness' knob: dev, staging, prod. In prod, anchor-missing is fatal; in dev it surfaces as a warning.

References (links we often mention)
----------------------------------
- Confluence spec (proto): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PROD/pages/12345678
- GH prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/hosted-api/pull/438
- Jira epic: INFR-724

Next meeting
------------
- 2025-11-21 09:00 PT - 30m sync to review CLI PoC and runbook.

Quick decision log
------------------
- Agreed: DSL is an opt-in annotation layer over existing JSON Schema for the first iteration.
- Agreed: Linter will live in infra/tools/schema-lint and be published as a GH Action & npm/pip package.

Footnote (for clarity)
---------------------
This doc is intentionally pragmatic. Goal is to get a small loop (linter -> mapping -> SDK adapter) into dev hands quickly so we can iterate on false-positive tuning before expanding rule coverage.
